definitions.explanation: The state of eagerly waiting and hoping for something to happen. Most commonly used as a modifier (待望の〜) to describe something people have been looking forward to.

examples.japanese: {待望|たいぼう}の{新作|しんさく}が{発売|はつばい}された。
examples.english: The long-awaited new release went on sale.

examples.japanese: {夫婦|ふうふ}に{待望|たいぼう}の{第一子|だいいっし}が{誕生|たんじょう}した。
examples.english: The couple's long-awaited first child was born.

examples.japanese: ファンが{待望|たいぼう}していた{来日公演|らいにちこうえん}が、ついに{実現|じつげん}することになった。
examples.english: The Japan concert that fans had been eagerly awaiting is finally going to happen.

notes:
USAGE:
Most frequently appears as a noun modifier: {待望|たいぼう}の〜 (the long-awaited ~). Also used as a suru verb ({待望|たいぼう}する = to eagerly await), though the modifier form is far more common. This word always carries a positive tone — the thing awaited is desired and welcome.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {待望|たいぼう}の{新作|しんさく}: long-awaited new work
- {待望|たいぼう}の{第一子|だいいっし}: long-awaited first child
- {待望|たいぼう}の{優勝|ゆうしょう}: long-awaited championship victory
- {待望|たいぼう}の{来日|らいにち}: long-awaited visit to Japan
